title: The First Cities
objective: After this level you can describe early cities like Uruk.
summary: Childe listed signs of the first cities: size, big public works, writing, full-time specialists. By about 3200 BCE Uruk had them all, and its first writing was bookkeeping.

cards.headline: Around 3200 BCE, the biggest settlement on Earth may have been in Iraq.
cards.body: It was Uruk, in southern Mesopotamia, in what is now southeastern Iraq. But a big crowd of houses isn't automatically a city. So what turns a settlement into one? Archaeologists have a checklist, and Uruk ticks the boxes.

cards.headline: A checklist for a city
cards.body: The archaeologist V. Gordon Childe listed 10 signs of the earliest cities. Among them: a bigger settlement than any village, large-scale public works, writing, and full-time specialists, people who do one job all day instead of farming. Think of it as a city's ID card. A village has houses. A city has houses plus a temple crew, a scribe and a wall builder.

cards.headline: Mud brick, dressed up
cards.body: Uruk's public works were monumental buildings of mud brick. Their walls were covered in mosaics made from painted clay cones, pressed in like pushpins in a corkboard. Around the whole city ran brick walls about 10 km long. Legend says the hero Gilgamesh built them. Whoever did, it took a great many bricks.

cards.context: The earliest written records in Sumerian are picture-sign tablets from Uruk, from about the end of the 4th millennium BCE. They aren't poems or prayers. They're lists and ledgers of goods, with numbers and names. A city full of specialists has to keep track of who handed over what. The first writers were, in effect, accountants.

cards.headline: The first cities: founded
learned: Childe's signs: size, public works, writing, specialists
Uruk, about 3200 BCE: largest settlement of its time
Mud-brick buildings clad in clay-cone mosaics

questions.prompt: Which of these is on V. Gordon Childe's list of signs of the earliest cities?

options.label: A population of exactly 10,000
options.rationale: Childe listed kinds of evidence, not a set population.

options.label: Paved car parks
options.rationale: Cars are a very modern problem.

questions.explanation: Childe's 10 signs include larger settlements, large-scale public works, writing and full-time specialists.

questions.prompt: What did the earliest tablets from Uruk mostly record?

options.label: Myths about the gods
options.rationale: Those came later; the first tablets were ledgers.

options.label: Laws for the whole city
options.rationale: Written law codes came much later.

options.label: Maps of the city's streets
options.rationale: The tablets are lists of goods with numbers and names.

questions.explanation: The earliest Sumerian writing is picture-sign tablets from Uruk that list goods, with numerals and names: a city's bookkeeping.

questions.prompt: Uruk's monumental buildings were made of a material Level 6 called one of the first building materials. Which?

options.label: Glass
options.rationale: Big glass walls came with iron frames (Level 8).

questions.explanation: Uruk's temples were mud brick, one of the first building materials, first made in sun-dried form at least 6,000 years ago.
